rule.body: Spelling does not always show the consonant sound. 'th' is /θ/ in thin but /ð/ in this. /ʃ/ is in ship, /tʃ/ in chip and /ʒ/ in measure. Some letters are silent: k in knee, b in debt, p in psalm, h in honest, s in island. 'ch' is /k/ in chemist and choir. The ending -ed is /ɪd/ after t or d (wanted), /t/ after other voiceless sounds (walked) and /d/ after other voiced sounds (played). The letter s is often /z/, as in rose and lose.
rule.example: wanted ends in /ɪd/, walked ends in /t/ and played ends in /d/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that begins with the sound /ð/, as in 'this'.
questions.explanation: those begins with voiced /ð/; thin, thank and thumb begin with voiceless /θ/.

questions.stem: In which word is the letter 'h' silent?
questions.explanation: honest is said /ˈɒnɪst/ with a silent h; house, hand and hill begin with /h/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that begins with the sound /ʃ/.
questions.explanation: shoe begins with /ʃ/; chip and cheap begin with /tʃ/, and jump with /dʒ/.
chemist begins with /k/; church, chair and cheese begin with /tʃ/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that contains the sound /ʒ/.
questions.explanation: measure has /ʒ/; pressure and mission have /ʃ/, and question has /tʃ/.

questions.stem: In which word is the '-ed' ending pronounced /ɪd/?
questions.explanation: wanted ends in /ɪd/ because the verb ends in t; walked and washed end in /t/, played in /d/.

questions.stem: In which word is the '-ed' ending pronounced /t/?
questions.explanation: laughed ends in /t/ after voiceless /f/; begged and rained end in /d/, needed in /ɪd/.

questions.stem: In which word is the letter 'p' silent?
questions.explanation: psalm is said /sɑːm/, so its p is silent; the p is sounded in pump, paper and open.

questions.stem: In which word is the letter 's' pronounced /z/?
questions.explanation: lose ends in /z/ (/luːz/); loose, case and dose end in /s/.

questions.stem: In which word is 'ch' pronounced the same way as in [[choir]]?
questions.explanation: choir and character begin with /k/; chain and child have /tʃ/, and machine has /ʃ/.
